chunkKeys.match: case-insensitive over the four ASCII bytes; both spellings are ordinary ancillary chunks

payloadForms.png: a complete PNG file; returned byte-for-byte, its own IHDR naming its dimensions
payloadForms.raw: exactly width*height 8-bit grey bytes, dimensions taken from the OUTER IHDR, which must therefore precede the depth chunk

pack.why: the writer (web/src/pack.ts) is a SECOND implementation of this format. The output file and the chunk's exact bytes (length, type, data and CRC) are pinned here because the readers walk by length and none of them validates a CRC: a wrong CRC would be silently skipped by a strict reader and accepted by a lenient one, which is depth on one machine and none on another. The colour is a gradient and the depth is a different gradient so a re-encoded colour or a swapped payload cannot match by accident.
pack.placement: before the first IDAT, after IHDR
pack.rule: a PNG input is never re-encoded: the output is the input byte-for-byte with one chunk inserted, and any existing dePH/dEPt chunk replaced rather than duplicated

status.ok: a depth map was recovered (form says which kind)
status.not-png: the input is not a PNG file at all
status.no-depth-chunk: a PNG was walked and no well-formed dePH/dEPt chunk was found
status.bad-payload: a depth chunk was found but its payload is neither a PNG nor the exact raw size
status.java: DepthPng.extract answers null for all three refusals: the app only ever asks 'is there depth', so the Java API does not distinguish them. The JS API does, and the JS test pins the specific code.

why: The app (Java) and the reference port (JS) both read this chunk out of a photograph, and each derives a depth map the renderer draws. A disagreement in what is accepted is a photograph that is 3D on the phone and flat on the web, or the reverse, with no error on either side.

cases.why: the ordinary form: raw 8-bit grey, exactly width*height bytes, under the spec-compliant key dePH
a complete PNG payload is passed through byte-for-byte, never re-encoded
dEPt is the other accepted spelling, in a different case again: matching is case-insensitive on the four ASCII bytes
all-caps DEPH is accepted too — the key is compared lowercased, not by an exact string
one byte too many for raw grey is REFUSED rather than resized or padded: a chunk and an image that disagree about dimensions cannot both be right
an empty chunk is a refusal, not an empty depth map — an all-zero map would render flat with no error
raw grey takes its dimensions from IHDR, so the same payload placed BEFORE IHDR claims nothing and is refused; a whole-PNG payload would still be accepted there
a four-byte key that is not dePH/dEPt in any case is not a depth chunk at all
a valid PNG with no depth chunk: "no depth" is the honest answer, and it must not be confused with a refusal
the signature check is the first gate; a non-PNG is not a PNG with no depth
a chunk that runs past the end of the file is malformed, so the walk stops; it must not throw, and it must not read past the buffer
the writer's input: a valid colour PNG with no depth chunk. Packing it must insert exactly one chunk and change no other byte
the writer's output: raw grey depth under dePH, inserted before the first IDAT and after IHDR, with the colour bytes untouched — the `pack` block above pins this file and the chunk byte for byte
